article.story: OXFORD, Miss. -- — Santiago Trouet came off the bench and scored 16 points to propel Mississippi to a lopsided 76-41 victory over Nicholls on Tuesday night. Trouet was the lone Rebel to reach double figures, making 4 of 7 shots from the floor and 8 of 9 free throws. Ole Miss grabbed the lead on baskets by Corey Stephenson and Patton Pinkins, then the Rebels scored 22 straight points for a 26-2 advantage. Trouet scored in the paint with 2 seconds left to put Ole Miss up 34-9 at halftime. Pinkins and Trouet accounted for the first four points of the second half, and Ole Miss was never threatened. Doyel Cockrill III made two 3-pointers and scored 10 to lead the Colonels (2-3). The Rebels shot 42% overall but missed 17 of 20 from 3-point range. They went 11 for 14 at the foul line. Nicholls shot 30%, made 6 of 25 from beyond the arc and 7 of 13 free throws. Ole Miss outrebounded the Colonels 49-32, with 18 of them coming at the offensive end, leading to 12 second-chance points. The Rebels also had a 22-2 advantage in fast-break points. Up next Nicholls will play Southern Mississippi on Saturday at the Pensacola Invitational. Mississippi plays Clemson on Monday at the Maui Invitational. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
